clue.text: See 7
King in the end turned over, work for emperor

indicators.note: the king's letter is placed within the flipped word
turned over says the word for end is flipped backwards in this down light

parts.note: an end is a goal or aim
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
to do is to work or perform

explanation.surface: An instruction for an emperor: kings toppled, work to be done.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned over' reverses AIM to MIA, and K goes 'in' it to make MIKA. The Mikado is also a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta, a play on 'work'.
explanation.definitionFit: Mikado is the old title of the emperor of Japan.

clue.text: Nothing between the ears, given a crown

indicators.note: between says the zero goes inside the word for ears

parts.note: ears of a cereal crop are corn
O, the round zero, stands for nothing

explanation.surface: An empty-headed person is nonetheless given a crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing between the ears' reads as an insult for a dim person, but the ears are ears of corn.
explanation.definitionFit: A corona is a crown, from the Latin word for it, and a crown-shaped ring of light.

clue.text: You look Labour's Tony up, bound by an old queen

indicators.note: bound by says the reversed run is enclosed by the letters of an
up in a down light says the words for you, look and the politician are read bottom to top

parts.note: ye is the old form of you
lo is an old word meaning look or behold
Tony Benn was a well-known left-wing Labour politician

explanation.surface: Someone invites you to look up a Labour politician named Tony, constrained by an old queen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Labour's Tony' suggests Blair, but it is Tony Benn. 'up' reverses YE LO BENN to NNEBOLEY, 'bound by' AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Anne Boleyn was the second wife of Henry VIII and queen of England, executed in 1536.

clue.text: Insect ineffective after head transplant

indicators.note: after head transplant says the first letter of the phrase for ineffective is swapped for another

parts.note: something of no use is ineffective

explanation.surface: A bug that fails to work even after surgery on its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after head transplant' swaps the N at the head of NO USE for L, a letter the clue leaves the crossings to supply.
explanation.definitionFit: A louse is a small wingless parasitic bug living on animals and people.

clue.text: Paparazzo's supporter on back page in a temper

indicators.note: in says the reversed word and page letter go inside the word for temper

parts.note: a mood is a temper, a bad humour

indicators.note: back says the word on is read the other way

explanation.surface: A celebrity photographer's backer, on the back page, is in a rage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns ON into NO.
explanation.definitionFit: A monopod is a one-legged camera stand, the kind press photographers use to steady long lenses.

clue.text: See 23
The usual: warm lager, no question — 25!

annotationWithheld.why: The usual: warm lager, no question — 25! (4): the only parse uses the cross-reference '25' (BOTTOMS UP) as both the last-letters indicator and the reversal indicator, one word doing two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: The usual: warm lager, no question — 25!

clue.text: Royal gaining publicity with menfolk: each is mixed up in relatively unpleasant crime

parts.note: PR stands for public relations, the business of publicity

indicators.note: the shuffled letters sit inside the word for the crime

parts.note: a crime committed between relatives: a playful description of incest

indicators.note: mixed up says the letters of menfolk, each and is are scrambled

explanation.surface: A royal attracts press attention among the men of a family caught up in a shameful scandal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relatively unpleasant crime' means a crime within the family. Princess Michael of Kent married Prince Michael, a cousin of Queen Elizabeth II.
explanation.definitionFit: She is a member of the British royal family by marriage, so a royal.

clue.text: Essence of a setter, perhaps, to be menial

parts.note: a setter is a breed of dog, so belonging to a dog, with perhaps flagging an example
body is substance or the main essential part

explanation.surface: The real nature of a crossword compiler is to be a lowly drudge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'setter' points at the puzzle's compiler, but here it is the gun dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A dogsbody is a drudge given the lowly tasks, a menial worker.

clue.text: Unanswerable question about religious leader in holy book

indicators.note: about says the riddle word goes round the leading letter

parts.note: a koan is a Zen Buddhist riddle with no logical answer

indicators.note: leader takes the first letter of religious

explanation.surface: A puzzling question about a cleric found in scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Koran is the sacred scripture of Islam.

clue.text: Subordinate serving dinner with glue, almost coming unstuck

indicators.note: coming unstuck says the letters of dinner and the shortened glue fall apart and rearrange
almost says the last letter of glue is dropped

explanation.surface: A junior waiter serves a meal made with glue that is falling apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims GLUE to GLU, and 'coming unstuck' rearranges DINNER GLU.
explanation.definitionFit: An underling is a person of lower rank, a subordinate.

clue.text: Insect finds sugar plant in girl's skirts buried in the sand

indicators.note: buried in says the inner assembly goes inside the sand word

parts.note: a dune is a ridge of sand

indicators.note: in says the plant sits within the girl's outer letters
skirts are the edges, so the outer letters of girl

parts.note: sugar beet is a plant grown for sugar

explanation.surface: A bug discovers a sugar crop hidden in a girl's skirt buried on the beach.
explanation.walkthrough: 'skirts' gives GL, the outsides of 'girl'; BEET goes 'in' them, and the lot is 'buried in' DUNE.
explanation.definitionFit: A dung beetle is a beetle that feeds on and rolls balls of animal droppings.

clue.text: Crust sliced carefully, accompanying butter for starters

indicators.note: for starters says take the opening letter of each of the four words

explanation.surface: Advice to slice a crust carefully and serve it with butter as an appetiser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crust' suggests bread, but it is a crust on a wound.
explanation.definitionFit: A scab is the dried crust that forms over a healing wound.

clue.text: Cursed devil, prowler in the grass

parts.note: an imp is a little devil

indicators.note: in says the prowling animal sits inside the grass word

parts.note: a reed is a tall grass of wetlands
a cat is a typical prowler

explanation.surface: A devilish prowler lurking in the long grass swore.
explanation.definitionFit: To imprecate is to call down evil on someone, so imprecated means swore or uttered curses.

clue.text: Then just escape and one is in the sea

parts.note: to leg it is to run away
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: in says the word is goes inside the sea word

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea

explanation.surface: Someone makes a run for it and ends up swimming in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'then just': made lawful in the past.
explanation.definitionFit: To legitimise is to make lawful or valid, so legitimised means rendered just at an earlier time.

clue.text: Plant turns into stick

indicators.note: into says the turns go inside the stick word

parts.note: to gel is to set or stick together
rounds are turns, as in a game

explanation.surface: A plant twists around a supporting stick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stick' looks like a noun, a cane, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Groundsel is a common weed of the daisy family.

clue.text: Sweet singer with posh name of writer

parts.note: Cher is a famous American pop singer
U means upper class in British usage
Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen, a writer

explanation.surface: A charming vocalist with an upper-class author's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'writer' suggests an author, but it is a Bic ballpoint pen.
explanation.definitionFit: Cherubic means angelic and childlike, so sweet in looks or manner.

clue.text: Animal near to doctor, squeezing nipple

indicators.note: squeezing says the rearranged letters hold the nipple word inside
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters of near are rearranged

parts.note: a teat is a nipple

explanation.surface: An animal comes close to its vet, squeezing a teat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to doctor' rearranges NEAR to ANER, 'squeezing' TEAT.
explanation.definitionFit: The anteater is a toothless mammal of Central and South America that feeds on ants.

clue.text: Newlywed found something sticky behind shower?

parts.note: honey is a sticky substance
a mooner shows off their backside, so is a shower of a behind

explanation.surface: A newly married person finds something sticky behind the shower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind shower' reads as a place, but it is someone who shows their behind.
explanation.definitionFit: A honeymooner is someone on the holiday taken just after marrying.

clue.text: See 7
Even bits of pencil show something long and thin

indicators.note: even bits says take the second, fourth and sixth letters of pencil

parts.note: to air is to show or broadcast

explanation.surface: Even shavings from a pencil look long and thin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'something long and thin' sounds like a pencil, but it is a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: An eclair is a finger-shaped choux pastry, filled with cream and topped with chocolate.

clue.text: Hum, while doing the backstroke in Lake Erie?

indicators.note: doing the backstroke says read backwards, as swimmers on their backs go
in says the letters sit within lake erie

explanation.surface: A bad smell while swimming on your back in Lake Erie.
explanation.definitionFit: Hum is British slang for a bad smell, so a stink.

clue.text: Broad characters in Spartacus, fine picture to broadcast

indicators.note: to broadcast is to scatter, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the closing three letters within the name Spartacus
pic is short for picture

explanation.surface: A broad view of Spartacus, a fine film to be shown on TV.
explanation.walkthrough: 'characters in Spartacus' gives CUS; 'to broadcast' rearranges CUS FINE PIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Unspecific means general or vague, not narrow, so broad.

clue.text: Character expecting father to overcome average fashion socialite

indicators.note: to overcome in a down light says father sits on top of average

parts.note: Pip is the hero of Dickens's novel Great Expectations
pa is father
middle means average or medium
ton means fashion or style, from French

explanation.surface: A pregnant woman hopes father will rise above being average in fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Character expecting' suggests a pregnant woman, but means the hero of Great Expectations. Pippa Middleton is the sister of Catherine, Princess of Wales.
explanation.definitionFit: She is a well-known British socialite and columnist.

clue.text: Game of the Royal Mint?

definitions.meaning: famously the sport of the British royal family
A brand of ring-shaped mint sweet in Britain

explanation.walkthrough: 'Royal Mint' reads as the coin factory, but it splits into two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Polo is a horseback ball sport and also a mint sweet with a hole in it.

clue.text: Tops down, then, bringing cheers

definitions.meaning: if tops are down, then the bottoms are up

explanation.walkthrough: Read 'tops down' literally: bottoms are up.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottoms up is a toast said before drinking, like cheers.

clue.text: Foreign letter in the midst of detail

indicators.note: midst of says take the two central letters of detail

explanation.surface: A letter from abroad sits in the middle of the fine print.
explanation.definitionFit: Theta is the eighth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Author right in tune with literature, primarily

indicators.note: in says right goes inside the tune

parts.note: a carol is a song or tune

indicators.note: primarily takes the first letter of literature

explanation.surface: An author got the tune right in combination with literature.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis Carroll was the writer of Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.

clue.text: Waste rejected by car inspector

indicators.note: by says the reversed word sits beside the car

parts.note: Audi is a German make of car

indicators.note: rejected says the word for waste is turned back

parts.note: rot is decay, waste

explanation.surface: Waste is turned away by a car inspector.
explanation.definitionFit: An auditor inspects financial accounts.
